01a0d4d7-fdc7-7f51-b2ba-8fd24cd63473.message:
Observed under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`:

```text
- Settings is roomier and easier to scan: sections are grouped with icons in the sidebar, each page has a clear title, and every setting sits on its own row with its switch or button on the right.
- OpenCode workers keep working when OpenCode 2 has taken over the `opencode` command: they find your OpenCode 1 install, and if there isn't one, the task stops straight away and says what to do instead of failing with an unrecognized flag. A worker can also point at a specific OpenCode 1 install.
- OpenCode 2 workers work again with OpenCode 2.0 and later, even when that install has also taken over the `opencode` command. Tasks, follow-ups, the model list with its effort levels, and continuing a task in a terminal all work, and a worker can point at a specific OpenCode 2 install.
- Picking a task from the list now puts you straight in its reply box.
- ⌘B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux) now shows or hides the task list, and puts you right in it so the arrow keys move between tasks.
- The reply box is simpler: task details and options now live behind the + button, so typing your next message is the only thing in the way.
- Settings can now pick the worker for you: turn on Choosing a worker, paste your TypeSafe key, and work you hand over without naming a worker lands on the one whose strengths fit what you asked for. Your own rules still catch anything it can't answer, and the task shows which worker was suggested and whether the work went there.
- Claude workers can now run newer models, like Opus 5.5, by using the Claude Code already installed on your machine instead of the older copy Oga shipped with.
- A task no longer fails with a confusing error when it starts just as Oga itself is starting up.
- The reply box no longer jumps when the note about continuing a paused task appears, and that note now lines up with the options under the box.
- Text in a task's activity log — command output, labels, and the response — now reads at one consistent size instead of jumping between sizes.
```

Inspected `/Users/malico/desgn/oga/CHANGELOG.md` using `oga query "CHANGELOG.md Unreleased heading"` and `rg -n '^## ' CHANGELOG.md && sed -n '/^## Unreleased$/,/^## /p' CHANGELOG.md`. No files changed.

item.text:
## TL;DR

- Three read-only subagents completed the requested repo survey.
- All three ran in parallel using `multi_agent_v1__spawn_agent` and `multi_agent_v1__wait_agent`.
- No files changed; no builds or tests were run.

## A

`rust/crates/` contains 16 crates:

- `oga-acp` — ACP transport and sessions.
- `oga-advisor` — Selects workers and effort levels.
- `oga-client` — Shared typed broker client.
- `oga-config` — Profiles and YAML settings.
- `oga-context` — Project code index.
- `oga-domain` — Shared domain types and JSON.
- `oga-events` — Task event normalization and storage.
- `oga-http` — Axum HTTP routes.
- `oga-mcp` — Stateless MCP server.
- `oga-pricing` — Provider spend estimates.
- `oga-providers` — Provider commands and transcript parsing.
- `oga-routing` — Task classification and model selection.
- `oga-runner` — Provider processes and cancellation.
- `oga-service` — Task orchestration and lifecycle.
- `oga-store` — SQLite persistence.
- `oga-worktree` — Git worktree lifecycle.

## B

- `index.ts` — Exports activity types, handoff types, activity composition/duration helpers, normalization functions, constants, `ActivityStory`, and `ActivityStoryProjection`.
- `index.test.ts` — No exports; activity composition and projection tests.
- `acp.test.ts` — No exports; ACP narration and provider-event tests.
- `fixtures/antigravity-acp-probe.json` — 15-row fixture.
- `fixtures/antigravity-run.jsonl` — 20-line fixture.
- `fixtures/claude-acp-resumed.json` — 521-row fixture.
- `fixtures/probe-rows.json` — Provider probe fixture object.

## C

Under `## Unreleased`:

- Settings is roomier and easier to scan: sections are grouped with icons in the sidebar, each page has a clear title, and every setting sits on its own row with its switch or button on the right.
- OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 workers now work with their respective installations, including explicit install selection and clearer failures.
- Picking a task now focuses its reply box.
- `⌘B`/`Ctrl+B` toggles the task list and focuses it for keyboard navigation.
- The reply box is simpler, with details and options behind `+`.
- Settings can automatically choose a worker using a TypeSafe key.
- Claude workers support newer models through the installed Claude Code.
- Tasks no longer fail confusingly during Oga startup.
- The paused-task continuation note no longer shifts the reply box.
- Activity-log text now uses a consistent size.
